plan: v2.8 44 G14: 30 scripted turns over a story with four rumors (true and false versions) that reach the receiver as hearsay; characters repeat them aloud as hearsay, nothing in the transcript ever witnesses one. After the run no rumor claim or version may stand as a fact, a [knows] row, canon or a chapter consequence. Invented names only; {receiver} and {narrator} are card names filled at run time.

story.title: SO-V44 G14 No Promotion
story.description: v2.8 plan 44 G14 fixture: four rumors reach the receiver as hearsay over 30 turns; two chapters so a seal runs.

rumors.claim: the ferry sank in the night

versions.text: the ferry sank and the ferryman drowned
rats have eaten half the winter grain in the granary

rumors.claim: the lord's son is coming home

versions.text: the lord's son died at the border fort
the lord's son was knighted at the border fort

rumors.claim: the old mine on the hill is haunted

versions.text: the old mine on the hill is full of silver nobody has found

qualities.rubric: Has talk of the ferry started in town?
Has talk of the granary started in town?
Has talk of the lord's son started in town?
Has talk of the old mine started in town?
Has the party left the town on the coast road?

checkpoints.name: The market town
checkpoints.objective: Gather supplies and news before the journey.

turns.player: I step off the coach into the rain and look for {receiver}.
turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: {receiver} waves from under the inn's awning and takes your bag.

turns.player: I ask {receiver} where we can buy rope and lamp oil.
turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The chandler's shop across the square is still open, its window fogged with lamp light.

turns.player: I buy a coil of rope and a flask of lamp oil.
turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: {receiver} counts out the coins for the oil and tucks the flask into a satchel.

turns.player: I suggest we get a hot meal at the inn.
turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The common room is crowded and loud, smelling of stew and wet wool.

turns.player: I find us a table near the fire.
turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: {receiver} leans close. I heard the ferry sank and the ferryman drowned, though nobody here saw it happen.

turns.player: I eat my stew and watch the room.
turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: A fiddler starts a slow tune in the corner, and a few patrons hum along.

turns.player: I ask the innkeeper about a room for the night.
turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The innkeeper, a broad man named Fenwick, hands over a brass key for the room at the top of the stairs.

turns.player: I thank Fenwick and carry our bags upstairs.
turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: {receiver} drops onto the narrow bed and pulls off a muddy boot.

turns.player: I open the shutters to look at the rain.
turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Below the window, two porters argue that, they say, rats have eaten half the winter grain in the granary.

turns.player: I close the shutters and blow out the candle.
turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The night passes with rain on the roof and the creak of the old inn.

turns.player: In the morning I go down for breakfast.
turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: {receiver} is already at the table, tearing a loaf of bread in half.

turns.player: I ask {receiver} what the town is talking about today.
turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: {receiver} shrugs. Someone told me the lord's son died at the border fort, and someone else says he was knighted there. Pick your story.

turns.player: I finish my tea and stand.
turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Outside, the rain has eased to a drizzle and the market stalls are opening.

turns.player: I walk to the market with {receiver}.
turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: A fishmonger named Petra calls out prices for eel and herring.

turns.player: I buy dried fish for the road.
turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: {receiver} haggles the fishmonger down by two coppers and grins.

turns.player: I look for a map seller.
turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: A map seller named Quillon unrolls a chart of the coast road on his stall.

turns.player: I buy the coast road map from Quillon.
turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: {receiver} traces the road on the map with a finger and stops at a bend marked with a cliff.

turns.player: I ask Quillon whether the coast road is safe.
turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Quillon says the road is safe in daylight, and that people claim the old mine on the hill is full of silver nobody has found, which is why fools wander off the road.

turns.player: I roll the map up and put it in my coat.
turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: {receiver} snorts. Silver in the old mine, they say. Gossip like that gets people lost.

turns.player: I check the horses at the stable.
turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The stable boy has brushed both horses, and the grey one nickers at you.

turns.player: I pay the stable boy and give the grey an apple.
turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: {receiver} tightens the girths and checks each hoof for stones.

turns.player: I ask {receiver} whether we have everything.
turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: {receiver} lists rope, oil, fish, bread, the map, and nods.

turns.player: I go back to the inn to settle the bill.
turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Fenwick takes your coins and wishes you a dry road.

turns.player: I thank Fenwick and step outside.
turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The bell of the town hall rings ten, and the drizzle stops.

turns.player: I mount the grey horse.
turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: {receiver} swings up onto the brown horse and settles the satchel.

turns.player: I ride with {receiver} toward the town gate.
turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The gate guards wave you through without a second look.

turns.player: I look back at the town once.
turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: {receiver} looks back too. Rumors and rain, that town. I will not miss either.

turns.player: I turn onto the coast road.
turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The coast road opens ahead, the sea grey and wide on your left.

turns.player: I ride on in silence for a while.
turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Gulls wheel over the cliffs, and the road climbs gently.

turns.player: I ask {receiver} how far the next village is.
turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: {receiver} squints at the map. Half a day, if the road stays dry.
